headline: Profit and margins slip despite a steady top line
summary_short: D.R. Horton's fiscal Q3 revenue was essentially flat y/y at $9,227.1M, while net income fell 12% to $904.9M and diluted EPS fell to $3.20 as homebuilding margins compressed; the company closed 23,983 homes, at the high end of its guidance range.
summary_long: Revenue was essentially flat y/y at $9,227.1M as 1% higher home-sales revenue (4% more homes closed) was offset by lower selling prices. Homebuilding pre-tax income fell 10% to $1.1B, with margin compressing to 12.3%, on cost growth outpacing revenue. Net income fell 12% to $904.9M and diluted EPS fell 5% to $3.20. The company returned $742.8M to shareholders via $615.7M of buybacks and $127.1M of dividends. Cash fell to $2,078.7M from $2,985.4M at fiscal-year start. D.R. Horton updated its FY2026 revenue and homes-closed guidance ranges and reiterated its cash-flow, buyback, and dividend targets.

drivers.explanation: Net income and EPS fell as homebuilding margins compressed even though revenue held flat; the company cited affordability constraints and cautious consumer sentiment weighing on demand, with incentives expected to stay elevated into Q4.
Home sales revenue rose 1% on 4% more homes closed, implying a lower average selling price; the release gives no explicit ASP figure or cause beyond the volume shown in its own tables.
Cost of sales rose faster than revenue at the homebuilding level, per the release's own segment tables, compressing gross profit despite roughly flat consolidated revenue.
Cost of sales grew 0.9% y/y against roughly flat revenue, consistent with the margin compression the release attributes to elevated incentives and cautious demand.
SG&A expense grew 5.0% y/y ($991.2M vs $944.3M) on flat revenue, per the release's consolidated income statement, compounding the gross-margin compression.

Tracks the EBIT decline; other (income) expense fell to $71.2M from $93.2M y/y, partly offsetting the operating decline, per the release's income statement.
Not explained beyond the homebuilding-segment margin compression to 12.3%; no specific cost driver is named for the consolidated net-income decline.
Tracks the net-income decline; diluted share count fell to 283.0M from 304.9M on buybacks, partly offsetting the earnings drop but not enough to prevent an EPS decline.
Tracks the same net-income decline as diluted EPS; basic share count fell to 282.2M from 304.1M on repurchases, per the release's disclosed share counts.
Cash fell as the company funded $2.2B of nine-month share repurchases and inventory growth from operating cash flow of $880.8M, per the release's cash-flow statement.

Retained-earnings growth from net income was outweighed by treasury-stock growth from buybacks (treasury stock rose to $12,620.1M from $10,431.1M at fiscal year start), per the release's balance sheet.
Share count fell on $2.2B of nine-month buybacks (14.6 million shares repurchased), per the release's own repurchase disclosure.
